findings.claim: The new contract text says the stream connection is shut down only once both halves are closed. The code also shuts it down when the peer sends EOF or the read fails, and when the parent client stops (abort_all_streams).
findings.basis: doc/rpc-streaming.md:115 and rpc_types.hh:340-342 versus the client::loop teardown and client::abort_all_streams in src/rpc/rpc.cc
mechanisms: The client loop runs `while (!_connected->read_buf.eof() && !_error)` and then calls stop_send_loop(ep) unconditionally, which shuts the socket and closes write_buf whatever the sink/source state is. abort_all_streams() calls abort() on every stream when the parent client stops. The commit message also says a half-closed stream 'is never shut down', which contradicts the corrected sentence at doc line 49 that closing the client aborts open streams.
findings.consequence: A user reading the docs may expect the connection to stay alive until both halves are closed, and misread a peer-initiated teardown or parent-close teardown as a bug. A future edit that relies on 'only once' (for example, keeping resources until stream_close) would be wrong.

evidence.detail: The stream loop exits on read_buf.eof() or _error.

findings.claim: The docs say reading the source until it throws closes it. Only exceptions from stream_receive() call close_source(). An exception from unmarshalling a buffer (process_one_buffer) propagates without closing the source.
findings.basis: doc/rpc-streaming.md:111 and rpc_types.hh:386-388 versus source_impl::operator() in rpc_impl.hh
mechanisms: process_one_buffer calls unmarshall<Serializer, In...>() outside the stream_receive then_wrapped that calls con->close_source(), so a deserialization exception leaves _source_closed false.
findings.consequence: An application that follows the docs and stops reading after a serializer exception leaves the source half open. stream_close() never runs, and nothing waits for the connection to stop, which is the leak the new docs are meant to prevent.

evidence.detail: unmarshall in process_one_buffer is not covered by close_source.
close_source() is called only when stream_receive fails or returns eof.

findings.claim: The regression test swallows closed_error and accepts a successful hook call too. It never checks that the hook is refused with closed_error, which is the new behavior the fix commit and the test commit both describe.
findings.basis: Commit 5e25ebdb message: 'With the fix the hook fails with closed_error and nothing is written.'
mechanisms: try { stream_send_empty_frame().get(); } catch (const rpc::closed_error&) {} has no BOOST_FAIL or flag on the success path. The test only checks put_after_close, which depends on the hook's frame reaching the parked data_sink.
findings.consequence: A future change that accepts the frame again but delays it until after data_sink::close() resolves would still pass, even though the frame would be written into a closed output_stream after the park is released.

evidence.detail: The hook result is not asserted to fail.
put_after_close is the only assertion.

findings.claim: No test covers the second half of the fix: stream_close() waiting for entries that send() accepted before _stream_closing was set.
findings.basis: Commit f545c28a adds the queue_drained wait as a separate mechanism; the PR body describes it as part of the fix.
mechanisms: The test calls the hook only after close_entered is set, so _stream_closing is already true and the queue is empty. The std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready, ...) and then_wrapped drain path, including its exceptional branch, never runs with a pending entry.
findings.consequence: A regression in the drain ordering, such as dropping the wait or mishandling a withdrawn or failed entry, would bring back the original unflushed-batch assertion without failing any test.

evidence.detail: The queue_drained.then_wrapped path ignores the exception and closes write_buf.
The hook is fired only after close() has been entered.

findings.claim: send() now refuses frames based on a second private flag, _stream_closing, but the public error() accessor still reports only _error. A connection can be refusing sends while error() returns false.
findings.basis: Callers such as sink_impl::send_buffer and sink_impl::close check con->error() before calling con->send().
mechanisms: send() checks `!_error && !_stream_closing`, while bool error() const noexcept { return _error; } is unchanged. Once stream_close() has begun, the two predicates disagree.
findings.consequence: A future caller that follows the existing pattern (check error(), then send) will get an unexpected closed_error ('connection is closed') on a connection that reports no error. Diagnosing that is confusing because the message says the connection is closed while error() is false.

evidence.detail: error() returns only _error.
send_buffer checks con->error() before con->send().

findings.claim: sink.close() and source eof now complete only after every frame queued before stream_close() has been written. The commit and PR do not mention this new completion dependency, and nothing can cancel it.
findings.basis: PR body says only that stream_close 'waits for _outgoing_queue to drain' as part of the fix. It says nothing about latency or cancellation for close_sink() and close_source() callers.
mechanisms: The compressor hook calls send({}) with no timeout and no cancellable, so its entries cannot be withdrawn. stream_close() chains write_buf.close() and then stop() behind queue_drained. If the front entry is stuck on TCP backpressure, sink.close() and the eof read wait, and stop() and shutdown_input() are delayed with them.
findings.consequence: An application waiting on sink.close() or the final source() read can see extra latency, or wait until the socket fails, when a compressor queued frames just before the close. This is uncertain: write_buf.close() could already block on flushing earlier data, so it may not be a real regression. Still, the docs added in commit 3 do not mention it.

evidence.detail: queue_drained is taken from _outgoing_queue_ready.
stop() runs only after f, which now includes the drain, completes.
The hook is send({}), with no timeout or cancel.
